clue.text: Carefully sorted out, like Dawkins's takings

definitions.meaning: chosen one by one with care, as the best items are selected
Jack Dawkins, the Artful Dodger in Dickens's Oliver Twist, is a pickpocket, so his loot is lifted from pockets by hand

explanation.surface: Something meticulously arranged is compared with the loot of a famous young thief.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawkins is not the biologist but Jack Dawkins, the Artful Dodger of Oliver Twist, a boy pickpocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: selected with care, and literally lifted by a pickpocket's fingers.

clue.text: Re-heated food in the mess

definitions.meaning: a dish of chopped, recooked leftover meat
a muddle or jumble, as in making a botch of something

explanation.surface: Leftovers warmed up and served in a military dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a dish of recooked chopped meat and a jumbled muddle.

clue.text: In France you and I show common sense

definitions.meaning: the French pronoun for 'we', that is you and I together

explanation.surface: A French couple demonstrate good practical judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: The French first-person plural pronoun is also the English informal word for practical wit.

clue.text: What have you in mind? This manual worker should know

definitions.text: What have you in mind? This manual worker should know

parts.words: What have you in mind? This manual worker should know
parts.note: the practitioner of a discredited Victorian pseudoscience felt the bumps of the skull with the hands to read character and mental faculties

explanation.surface: Someone asks what you are thinking, and a labourer is said to have the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual worker' suggests a labourer, but this person works literally by hand, feeling the head's bumps to read the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrenology claimed to read mental traits from the shape of the skull, felt by hand.

clue.text: Ionian island, half full with Corinthians

parts.note: COR is the usual abbreviation for the Bible book Corinthians

indicators.note: half signals taking only the first two of the four letters of the word full

explanation.surface: A Greek island is half packed with Corinthian visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Corinthians is a book of the New Testament; 'with' is only a joining word, and the island's name comes from its abbreviation followed by half a word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the Ionian Islands off the west coast of Greece.

clue.text: Get me a helper somehow temporary will do

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the three words are to be put together in some other way

explanation.surface: An employer short of staff will take anyone, even a stopgap assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of 'me a helper'; 'Get' and 'will do' are just joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting lasts only a short time, the sense of passing and short-lived.

clue.text: A block in the colon

definitions.meaning: a colon is a punctuation mark, which old-fashioned usage calls a kind of point

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding complaint about an obstruction in the bowel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colon' reads as the gut, but it is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an obstruction and also a punctuation mark such as a colon or full point.

clue.text: Cleaner comes by Tube, but won't go back in it

definitions.text: Cleaner comes by Tube, but won't go back in it

parts.words: Cleaner comes by Tube, but won't go back in it
parts.note: a dental cleaning product squeezed from a tube, which famously cannot be pushed back once out

explanation.surface: A domestic cleaner travels by the London Underground but refuses to ride home on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground; it is a squeezable container, and 'cleaner' is for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentifrice is a cleaner for teeth, sold in squeezable tubes.

clue.text: Critic looks unhealthy, eating rook in flaky confection

parts.note: Mr Puff is a character in Sheridan's comedy The Critic

indicators.note: eating means the pale-looking word takes the chess letter into its middle

parts.note: to look pasty is to look pale and unwell
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A reviewer who is looking off-colour scoffs a crumbly pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Critic' is not a reviewer in general: Mr Puff is the critic of Sheridan's play The Critic. 'eating' takes the chess abbreviation into the word for looking pale.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light dough rolled into many buttery layers that bake into flakes.

clue.text: Familiar greeting cut short by man from the landowners

indicators.note: cut short means the greeting loses its final letter

parts.note: 'squire' is a matey British form of address, as in 'All right, squire?'
Archy is a pet form of the man's name Archibald

explanation.surface: A matey hello is interrupted by someone from the landed classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last letter of SQUIRE to leave SQUIR. 'Squire' is a cheery British way to address a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The squirearchy is the class of country gentry who own landed estates.

clue.text: Beat in return game here

indicators.note: in return means the word for beat is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to flog is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Someone gets a beating back in a sporting rematch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns FLOG round; 'here' just points to the game.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sport played with clubs and a ball over a course of holes.

clue.text: Burning issue in film on the dole

indicators.note: on in a down clue places one piece above the next

parts.note: taken as written
cine is short for cinematograph, a film
a dole is a portion handed out, a ration

explanation.surface: A hot topic appears in a movie about unemployment benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning issue' looks like the phrase for a hot topic; 'issue' is a linking word and 'Burning' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning something to ashes is destruction by fire, the process in a furnace.

clue.text: Having a lead, crew may use this to keep it

definitions.text: Having a lead, crew may use this to keep it

parts.words: Having a lead, crew may use this to keep it
parts.note: the art of staying one step ahead of rivals, which a ship's crew might employ to stay in front

explanation.surface: Sailors in a race who are ahead use some tactic to stay there.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits the word into the idea of a lead and a vessel's crew; the whole is Stephen Potter's term for gaining a psychological edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamesmanship of keeping just ahead of others is the art of staying in front.

clue.text: Boy on unusually late in charge of postal collection

indicators.note: on in a down clue places one piece above the next

parts.note: Phil is a boy's name

indicators.note: unusually signals the four letters of late in an odd order

explanation.surface: A lad who is oddly late is put in charge of the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the four letters of 'late'; 'on' stacks the boy's name above the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp collecting is the hobby, so the adjective describes collecting postage stamps.

clue.text: The screwdriver for some craftsmen

parts.note: 'craft' here means ships, and the screw is a ship's propeller, driven from a compartment below deck

explanation.surface: A workshop tool used by artisans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftsmen' suggests artisans, but read as men of craft, ships' crews; the screw is the propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: The compartment holding a ship's motors powers the propeller, its screw.

clue.text: Sounds a foreign composer but for the big moustache

indicators.note: sounds means the composer's name is taken as said aloud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: Handel was a German-born composer
bar means except, as but does in 'all but one'

explanation.surface: A foreign composer's name is heard, but only in connection with a famous whiskered face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' gives the spoken name of the German-born composer Handel, spelt as the bar on a bicycle; 'but' is BAR, meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide moustache with curled ends resembles the steering bar of a bicycle.

clue.text: Side of the foot used for reverse

parts.note: the back is the rear side of something
pedal is the adjective relating to the feet

explanation.surface: A footballer uses the outside of a boot to play the ball backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedal' as an adjective means of the foot; 'used for' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat from a position is to pedal backwards, withdrawing a stance.

clue.text: They lead prayers for single mothers

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, gives single
mams is an informal word for mothers

explanation.surface: Some figures lead prayers on behalf of single mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the Muslim leaders who lead worship in a mosque.

clue.text: False horizontal

explanation.surface: A two-word description of a deceitful person lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means telling untruths and also flat on the ground.

clue.text: He assembles the other ranks after daily prayer

indicators.note: after places the soldiers' abbreviation behind the prayer

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer appointed for the day
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, the enlisted soldiers

explanation.surface: An officer gathers the troops after morning prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short Anglican prayer set for a given day; 'He assembles' is someone who gathers things.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gathers items into a set brings them together.

clue.text: Sorting out the ethical hoops of intuitive religion

indicators.note: sorting out means the letters of the two words are rearranged into order

explanation.surface: A philosopher untangles the moral obstacles of a mystical faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorting out' rearranges ETHICAL HOOPS; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical belief system claiming direct intuitive knowledge of the divine.

clue.text: Did I omit a characteristic expression? No!

indicators.note: the exclamation says nothing was left out: the expression is still there, sitting inside the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they left out a typical turn of phrase, and is told they did not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No!' answers the question: the expression was not omitted, it sits in 'Did I omit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of phrase peculiar to a language is a characteristic expression.

clue.text: Remarkable Scottish. university sergeant, say

parts.note: a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A Scottish university sergeant is said to be remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Scots for strange or remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means extraordinary or uncommon.

clue.text: A former railway charity.

parts.note: the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, a British company until 1948

explanation.surface: An old railway line has been turned into a charitable body.
explanation.walkthrough: The LMS was one of Britain's four big railway companies before nationalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or food given to the poor is charity.

clue.text: Spoil the game — start to throw

parts.note: loo is an old card game

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of throw is taken

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a game by beginning to throw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes T from 'throw'; loo is an old card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoils are plunder or booty, the goods taken by a looter.

clue.text: Putting two and two together, a Left supplementary

parts.note: putting numbers together is arithmetic summing

explanation.surface: Working something out, a left-wing politician offers an extra point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting two and two together' is literally arithmetic summing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extra is added on top, supplementing what is there.

clue.text: Affected by closure of atomic power unit

indicators.note: closure of means the final letter of atomic is taken

parts.note: an amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is affected by the shutdown of a nuclear plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closure of' gives C, the last letter of 'atomic'.
explanation.definitionFit: It means mannered and theatrical, exaggerated in style.

clue.text: Birdies mean golf is fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic suggests a fanciful reshaping of the letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A golfer exults that scoring under par makes golf wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdies' looks like a golf score; it means birds. 'fantastic' rearranges MEAN GOLF IS.
explanation.definitionFit: These pink wading birds are examples of birds, called birdies informally.
